deviations.title: twin_fade: layer fades differ from the design's group fade by up to 26 levels over the cover (within lead ruling R-b's bound of 28; 16 before the erratum) and 35 where the labels of two fading layers overlap (the volume reveals; within lead ruling R-g's bound of 36)
deviations.status: resolved: K1 errata of lead rulings R-b (<= 28 over the cover) and R-g (<= 36 where the labels of two fading layers overlap, the volume reveals); confirm both by eye in the hardware window (K1 15.4)
deviations.contract: PRESENTATION_V5.md 8.5.3 / 16.1 P5-13 and 15.3 twin_fade after the R-b and R-g errata (16.7 E-b, 16.8 E-g): <= 28 per channel inside label ink boxes over the cover, <= 36 where a label ink box of another layer fading in the same capture overlaps; no difference outside them
deviations.ruling: R-g (2026-09-26): a per-class bound of 36 for the volume-reveal overlap class (two text layers fading over 150-190 ms), R-b's bound unchanged for every other in-box pixel; the first option below, with a flat measured bound instead of the per-pixel model; confirmed by eye in the hardware window

over_the_cover.probe: v5-twin-fade content opa 94 +20: max |d| inside ink boxes 26 (over the cover 26; where a label of another fading layer overlaps 0, 0 px), outside 0 (0 px)

where_fading_layers_overlap.probe: v5-twin-fade volume opa 109 +120: max |d| inside ink boxes 35 (over the cover 25; where a label of another fading layer overlaps 35, 969 px), outside 0 (0 px)

cause: Over the cover (content, track and volume fades; worst 26 in the content fade, with 68 under the ink there): P5-13 models the error as 0.8a(1 - a) x what lies under the label (<= 15 for the <= 74.5 composite), 12.7 at that pixel. LVGL blends the twin and then the label into the RGB565 framebuffer, each blend rounded to 5/6-bit channels (a 5-bit step is 8.2 levels); the float model leaves that per-primitive arithmetic out, and it accounts for the rest.

Where the labels of two fading layers overlap (worst 35 in the volume fade, with 123 under the ink there; per layer {'track': 24, 'volume': 35}): the volume caption and the home title cross-fade in the same place in both volume reveals (K1 8.8). Reveal-out: the volume layer fades out over 170 ms while the track layer fades back in after 90 ms, so from +90 ms the caption lies over partly visible title ink, not the dark composite: the float model alone gives 24.1 at that pixel, above the 15 of P5-13 before any RGB565 rounding. Reveal-in: the caption fades in (after 50 ms) above the title fading out over 150 ms. P5-13 covers neither case, and a single bound set from the over-the-cover worst would still fail here.
options: A lead ruling for the overlap class only (R-b's 28 stays for the cover): a separate bound limited to labels of layers that fade in the same capture, derived from P5-13's model at each pixel rather than from the measured worst -- |d| <= 0.8a(1 - a) x u + R, with u the brightest channel under the label ink and R the RGB565 term (measured above the model: 14.1 over the cover, 17.4 in the overlap class); its worst case is the title ink under the caption at a = 0.5 (0.2 x 242 = 48.4, plus R). The difference is a slightly darker caption interior while the two labels cross-fade (volume 180/170 ms), to be confirmed by eye with the rest of R-b.

Remove the overlap: sequence the volume reveals so the two layers never fade at once (reveal-in: the volume fade-in after the track has faded out, delay 150 instead of 50 ms; reveal-out: the track fade-in after the volume has faded out, delay 170 instead of 90 ms). A K1 8.8 motion change for the design owner; the caption and title then no longer cross-fade, and R-b's one bound applies as written. Not measured in the harness.

Not an option: hiding the volume caption twin during the reveal-out. K1 8.5.3 rejected hiding twins during fades, and the shadow-edge pixels would then differ from the group reference by up to 0.8a x the ink under them, which fails the same check.

deviations.title: R5: a superseded cover decode stops at the next MCU band (K1 12.5.4 step 2, lead ruling R-f: cc_art_decode.cpp decodes with &cancelled through cc_jpeg.cpp's abort hook), so after a fast spin the resting cover arrives within one decode time plus one band of the last detent (K1 12.5.7(h))
deviations.contract: PRESENTATION_V5.md 12.5.4 step 2 (decode with &cancel; JDR_INTR at the next MCU band), 12.5.7 (h) and 12.5.7's jpeg_tests.py abort-at-every-band case
deviations.cause: src/cc_art_decode.cpp run() decodes with cc_jpeg_decode_240(stage, bytes, dst, &cancelled) and maps the result through cc_art_decode_result() (cc_art_decode.h: an abort the decoder saw stays aborted, never failed); cc_jpeg.cpp polls the flag between MCU rows (JDR_INTR, CC_JPEG_ABORTED, the decoder reusable; jpeg_tests.py aborts at every band of 24 samples). The harness fake stops at the next of 15 bands like it. Measured: 127 ms with 120 ms decodes (limit 129), 155 ms with 154 ms decodes (limit 166), 46 ms with 46 ms decodes (limit 51).
